executiveSummary: GM0687's 2025 identity, generalized boundary, centre, 50,152 residents, 72 neighbourhoods, three BAG places, nine BRT settlements, two stations and seven logical road-border links are internally coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Middelburg is an inland, low-lying Walcheren municipality protected by primary and regional defences whose coastal outcome depends on a named North Sea/Westerschelde/Oosterschelde/Veerse Meer boundary, breach or overtopping pathway, dikes/dues/coupures/locks, the Kanaal door Walcheren and a governed inundation surface. The canonical coastal preset instead emits 2.348448 m and 30,576 affected population-equivalent at T+24 without any of those dimensions; at T+72 depth and severity become zero while 4,960 remain under pressure. The river preset emits 0.413214 m at T+24–T+72 and more than 518,000 deprived person-hours while affected population remains zero, despite no selected major-river pathway. Pluvial T+24 emits 0.309254 m and 6,523 affected without rainfall, terrain, sewer, surface-water or outside-water state. Official Walcheren modelling shows that the Kanaal door Walcheren, Vlissingen/Veere discharge windows, Boreel/Poppekinderen pumping and high outside-water maalstop logic are coupled; the municipal system can overflow during extreme rain. Current Waterinfo assigns no point to GM0687, although the nearest boundary-relevant Oranjeplaat and Vlissingen observations/forecasts lie 3.54 and 7.32 km from the centre and forecasts stop at T+24. Public registers identify 77 water assets, Stedin/Evides territories, one grid-planning sample, 83 antenna sites, 41 education locations and no local acute hospital, but not live connectivity, capacity, backup, acceptance or recovery. A58's two graph edges are one non-additive corridor; Walcheren access also depends on N57, canal crossings, rail and cross-boundary ADRZ care in Goes. Exact hazards, service percentages and recovery must be suppressed or labelled synthetic until selected, time-valid scenarios and auditable first-72-hour action/resources exist; null, empty, stale and out-of-polygon data remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0687 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, safety-region and statistics inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs uniquely identify GM0687 as Middelburg (Z.) in Zeeland and Veiligheidsregio Zeeland, and report 50,152 residents, density 1,037/km², 23.3% aged 65 or older and 10,354 one-person households. The reference point [3.6626107496104545,51.49504460308661] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Seventy-two neighbourhoods in 24 districts sum to 50,155 residents, three above the municipal control (+0.006%); published households total 24,145 and rounded age-65-plus rows 11,700. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 50,152 without rewriting observations.

Three active BAG places are Arnemuiden, Middelburg and Nieuw- en Sint Joosland. Nine BRT labels comprise two deelkernen, two gehuchten and five woonkernen; these feature types are not interchangeable population controls. BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0.

District heating and charging are missing in all 72 neighbourhoods; cars per household is missing 30 times, home/tenure variables 21 times and benefit/distance/density fields also have gaps. Null/suppression remains NoData, not zero; annual residence omits commuters, tourists, students, care occupancy and transient Walcheren traffic.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Stedelijk Waterprogramma 2021–2030 and municipal water-overload evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Stedelijk Waterprogramma 2021–2030; current municipal pages and 2026 maintenance plan inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The programme distinguishes water nuisance from damaging water overload, identifies sewer and public-space bottlenecks and plans climate-adaptive renewal. It is policy/planning evidence, not a current event, completed works inventory or operational capacity source.

The municipality says its public sewer was not designed for the heaviest cloudbursts. On dry days two Middelburg sewer pumps and the Arnemuiden pump move more than 8 million litres/day to Ritthem; in all-day rain they can move up to about 80 million litres/day, while overloads discharge mixed wastewater/rain through overflows and more extreme rain can inundate streets, buildings and tunnels.

Those public explanatory values describe a network/design concept, not timestamped live flow, free storage, pump/plant availability, receiving-water head, water quality or T+72 performance. The 2026 works plan includes sewer relining, tunnel/bridge maintenance and further extreme-rain measures but not audit-time completion/access.

A permanent municipal groundwater network has 39 gauges across Middelburg, Arnemuiden, Nieuw- en Sint Joosland and Sint Laurens and specifically studies seepage along the Kanaal door Walcheren. Public gauge programme context is not a current municipality groundwater surface unless time-valid readings are ingested.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Hydrological research report Walcheren and public water-system assets
evidenceSources.edition: Hydrological report version 1.0 final dated 12 December 2017, adopted 28 June 2018; HWH asset snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026; report blanket reuse licence not stated, HWH CC BY-SA 4.0
supports: The official historic model describes Walcheren as a coupled polder system draining through Boreel, Poppekinderen and other pumps into the Kanaal door Walcheren and onward through Veere/Vlissingen controls. High outside water shortens discharge duration, raises canal level and can trigger pump maalstops; this mechanism is absent from an isolated rain/depth scalar.

The report identifies Dauwendaele and Middelburg-Zuid WB21 deficiencies and optimisation via connections, culvert enlargement and pumping changes. It also describes a Domburgse-Watergang control that reduces pumping when Middelburg's Vesten reach a threshold. These are 2017 model/planning facts, not proof of current configuration or performance.

The deployed HWH clip contains 77 realized records: three sewer pumps, one sluice, six surface-water pumps and 67 weirs. Sixty-nine capacities are null; eight values, including Boreel, Poppekinderen and three sewer pumps, have no displayed comparable unit/connectivity in the consumed schema.

Point/function/realized labels and historic model capacity are static context. They do not establish connected catchments, current pump/sluice/weir position, available capacity, outside-water head, electricity/backup, crew, maintenance, failure or restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Informatiehuis Water / WMCN / Provincie Zeeland / Waterschap Scheldestromen
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Current official flood-scenario, defence and regional-water reference sources
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO current portal/method version inspected 3 September 2026; Zeeland Water Programme amendment published 2025; Scheldestromen defence map service current; component licences vary and must remain attached
supports: LIWO contains professional flood and water-overload layers and explicitly requires specialist water-manager interpretation. Its 21 November 2025 methodology says global defence-failure estimates are not suitable for the warm phase; incident probability must use expected load, field observations and emergency measures.

The Waterveiligheidsportaal distinguishes statutory primary-defence norms, assessment results and strengthening projects. A need/assessment/project is neither a current failure nor a municipality-wide safety guarantee.

Zeeland's current programme distinguishes primary defences, always-water-retaining regional defences along the Kanaal door Walcheren/Veerse Meer and dry compartmentalising inland dikes. Buitendijkse areas lack the same norm/base-protection semantics.

Scheldestromen's public defence service exposes defence systems, coupures, sluices, pumps and other works. These are integration-ready geometry/context, not incident state. A decision-facing coastal run needs named outside-water source, breach/overtopping/coupure/lock state, scenario footprint, arrival/recession, uncertainty and release/licence.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Boundary-relevant water observations/forecasts and issued weather-warning context
evidenceSources.edition: Water observations valid 2 September 2026 17:30Z; forecasts retrieved 3 September 04:29Z; KNMI warning fallback issued 2 September 21:36Z; Waterinfo CC0, KNMI CC BY 4.0
supports: No Waterinfo point is assigned inside GM0687's generalized polygon. The nearest fresh observations are Arnemuiden Oranjeplaat at -3 cm NAP, 3.54 km from the municipal centre, and Vlissingen at +190 cm NAP, 7.32 km away, both publisher-classed normal; geographic non-assignment remains explicit rather than becoming no water.

Both locations have forecasts at T+1/+6/+12/+24 only. Oranjeplaat ranges -8 to -1 cm NAP and Vlissingen follows the tide from -107 to +222 cm NAP; no records exist for these points at T+48/T+72. Point normal/tidal values are not a breach, inundation, defence assessment or all-clear.

The Zeeland province warning record reports warning level zero/no warning with a 48-hour horizon. No local KNMI in-situ station record lies within GM0687. Warning absence/short horizon and missing local station never validate a synthetic T+72 coastal, storm, heat, winter, fire/smoke or recovery state.

Retain location/authority, water body, parameter, unit/datum, issue/valid/retrieval time, quality, horizon and out-of-polygon role; never extrapolate or convert boundary points directly into municipality depth.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — First-72-hour preparedness and shelter/evacuation guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Current authority guidance inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Zeeland Veilig advises at least 72 hours of household self-reliance and a kit including two litres of drinking water per person per day, shelf-stable food, first aid/medication, lighting/radio/batteries, cash and warm clothing. Guidance is not measured household stock or warning reach.

Current shelter/evacuation guidance at https://www.zeelandveilig.nl/wat-kan-ik-doen/in-en-om-het-huis/denk-na-over-schuilenevacueren notes that flood response may require vertical shelter/high ground, evacuation, shared transport and preparation for long traffic queues. It is general instruction, not an incident order, route allocation or reception capacity.

Scheldestromen's storm protocol uses forecast-water-level phases, monitoring, closing specified coupures/locks and field inspection; a published threshold/protocol is conditional planning, not current activation or completion.

No reviewed input supplies current command decision, warning acknowledgement, defence inspection/control, shelter/evacuation assignment, transport assistance, reception, resource stock, utility/care continuity or completed recovery.

evidenceSources.publisher: Nationaal Wegenbestand / ProRail / Provincie Zeeland / public-transit publishers
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Walcheren road, canal-crossing, rail and transit dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: Provincial mobility evidence published 2026; NWB August 2026, ProRail 2025 and GTFS snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; NWB/ProRail CC0, GTFS terms vary
supports: Seven logical edges connect Goes, Vlissingen and Veere via A58, N665, N661, N660, N663 and N57. The two A58 edges share one physical corridor and repeated 260-unit ceilings are consecutive/non-additive, not independent evacuation or supply capacity.

The province identifies Kanaal door Walcheren barrier effects, few crossings, bridge openings, rail crossings and limited alternative routes as persistent Middelburg/Vlissingen access vulnerabilities. Static graph adjacency does not capture these common-mode controls.

Two stations, Arnemuiden and Middelburg, plus 55 GTFS stop areas are valid geometry/schedule context. They do not establish event-time train/bus operation, canal crossing, vehicle/crew, passenger or freight throughput, emergency priority or T+72 service.

A58/Sloedam eastward, N57/Veerse Gatdam northward, N661 toward Vlissingen, canal bridges and the Zeeland rail line need mode/direction, physical corridor/control identity and issue/valid state. Zero bounded NDW records never means open.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / HWH / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public utility, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Public snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026 CC0; Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain, HWH CC BY-SA 4.0, DUO CC BY version unspecified; exact NBNL/RDI licences not established
supports: A centre-point lookup identifies Stedin electricity (record updated 24 March 2026), Stedin gas (17 December 2025) and Evides water (12 May 2026); drainage and media are empty. Territory is responsibility context, not network topology, redundancy, current outage or quality.

One Middelburg/Stedin planning sample has unknown existing/required MW, a 6.8 MW withdrawal queue with 17 requests, zero published injection queue and nine projects from 2027. It is large-user planning, not current load, reserve, switching state, damage or T+72 restoration.

RDI returns 83 antenna sites and DUO 41 education locations. Locations/counts do not prove radio coverage/backhaul/power, shelter designation, opening, occupancy, accessibility, staffing, supplies or generator endurance.

No acute hospital is registered inside GM0687. The nearest listed facility is ADRZ Goes at 17.03 km, reporting 24/7 emergency/acute obstetrics, 18 rooms and 28,921 visits in 2025; ZorgSaam De Honte is 24.86 km away. Straight-line distance/annual roles do not establish route time, acceptance, occupancy, staff, utilities, stock or surge.

findings.summary: The river preset reports depth and large service burden with zero affected people and no selected major-river pathway.
